nodes.description: The tumor secretes parathyroid hormone without normal calcium feedback, producing primary hyperparathyroidism with raised PTH and serum calcium.

evidence.reference_title: Mice deleted for cell division cycle 73 gene develop parathyroid and uterine tumours: model for the hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumour syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Cdc73+/-, Cdc73+/L/PTH-Cre and Cdc73L/L/PTH-Cre mice had higher mean serum calcium concentrations than wild-type littermates, and Cdc73+/- mice also had increased mean serum parathyroid hormone (PTH) concentrations.

nodes.description: Carriers are followed with serum calcium, intact PTH and 25-hydroxyvitamin D from childhood, with neck ultrasound, because biochemistry alone can miss parathyroid carcinoma in normocalcemic carriers.

evidence.reference_title: CDC73-Related Disorders.
evidence.snippet: Serum calcium, intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH), and 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels annually starting by age ten years. Periodic neck ultrasound as indicated based on serum calcium and iPTH levels.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis of parathyroid tumors in familial isolated hyperparathyroidism with HRPT2 mutation: implications for cancer surveillance.
evidence.snippet: Our experience suggests that longitudinal surveillance by serum biochemistry alone may not be 100% sensitive, and addition of routine neck ultrasonography is a readily accepted adjunct that may facilitate earlier disease detection in some families.

meta.association: Heterozygous germline inactivating variants (truncating point variants, missense variants and partial or whole-gene deletions) of the parafibromin gene. Germline CDC73 variants explain only a minority of FIHP kindreds overall.

evidence.reference_title: Familial isolated hyperparathyroidism is rarely caused by germline mutation in HRPT2, the gene for the hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Among the 32 FIHP families, only a single one was found to have a mutation in HRPT2 (679insAG); this mutation predicts premature truncation of its gene product, parafibromin, and thus its presumed inactivation.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic analyses in patients with familial isolated hyperparathyroidism and hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumour syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Germline mutations of HRPT2 were found in two of the 11 FIHP families and one of the two HPT-JT families.

evidence.reference_title: HRPT2-related familial isolated hyperparathyroidism: could molecular studies direct the surgical approach?
evidence.snippet: A nonsense mutation was found in exon 1 (c.96G>A)(p.Trp32X) in all affected members studied.

evidence.reference_title: Frequent large germline HRPT2 deletions in a French National cohort of patients with primary hyperparathyroidism.
evidence.snippet: Germline mutations of the HRPT2 gene (CDC73) coding for parafibromin are identified in approximately 50%-75% of HPT-JT cases and in approximately 14% of familial isolated hyperparathyroidism.

evidence.reference_title: Frequent large germline HRPT2 deletions in a French National cohort of patients with primary hyperparathyroidism.
evidence.snippet: Seven patients (35%) carried a gross deletion of this gene (3 complete and 4 partial deletions).

evidence.reference_title: Genetic or familiar forms of primary hyperparathyroidism: description of a case series with familial isolated hyperparathyroidism and review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Initial laboratory investigations revealed increased PTH and calcium levels, and cervical ultrasound identified a nodule suggestive of parathyroid enlargement.

nodes.description: A heterozygous germline variant inactivates one CDC73 allele in every cell. CDC73 encodes parafibromin, a component of the RNA polymerase II-associated PAF1 complex; most disease variants truncate the protein or delete the gene, and missense variants misfold its N-terminal domain.

evidence.reference_title: HRPT2, encoding parafibromin, is mutated in hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Our findings suggest that HRPT2 is a tumor-suppressor gene, the inactivation of which is directly involved in predisposition to HPT-JT and in development of some sporadic parathyroid tumors.

evidence.reference_title: Familial isolated hyperparathyroidism is rarely caused by germline mutation in HRPT2, the gene for the hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome.
evidence.snippet: this mutation predicts premature truncation of its gene product, parafibromin, and thus its presumed inactivation

evidence.reference_title: The HRPT2 tumor suppressor gene product parafibromin associates with human PAF1 and RNA polymerase II.
evidence.snippet: These interactions depend on a C-terminal domain of parafibromin, which is deleted in ca. 80% of clinically relevant mutations.

evidence.reference_title: The parafibromin tumor suppressor protein is part of a human Paf1 complex.
evidence.snippet: Like the yeast complex, the parafibromin complex associates with the nonphosphorylated and Ser2 and Ser5 phosphorylated forms of the RNA polymerase II large subunit.

evidence.reference_title: Crystal structure of the N-terminal domain of human CDC73 and its implications for the hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor (HPT-JT) syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Our crystal and biochemical data indicate that most CDC73 missense mutations disrupt the folding of the hydrophobic core of hCDC73-NTD, while others such as the K34Q mutant reduce its thermostability.

molecular_functions: parafibromin binding to RNA polymerase II within the PAF1 complex

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis of parathyroid tumors in familial isolated hyperparathyroidism with HRPT2 mutation: implications for cancer surveillance.
evidence.snippet: Biochemical and ultrasonographic evaluation uncovered a 27-yr-old hypercalcemic carrier niece with an atypical parathyroid adenoma

evidence.reference_title: Surveillance for early detection of aggressive parathyroid disease: carcinoma and atypical adenoma in familial isolated hyperparathyroidism associated with a germline HRPT2 mutation.
evidence.snippet: One of the siblings newly identified as mutation-positive was noted to be hypercalcemic at the time of the genetic screening.

nodes.description: Acute management of severe or symptomatic hypercalcemia. Dehydration should be avoided.

evidence.reference_title: CDC73-Related Disorders.
evidence.snippet: Intravenous fluids and a bisphosphonate infusion for severe or symptomatic hypercalcemia.

nodes.description: Parafibromin restrains proliferation through PAF1-complex repression of c-myc and suppression of cyclin D1, and promotes apoptosis. Its loss releases these restraints. These functions were established in cultured cell lines rather than in parathyroid tissue.
nodes.id: Loss of Parafibromin Antiproliferative and Proapoptotic Control

biological_processes: negative regulation of cell proliferation by parafibromin

evidence.reference_title: The parafibromin tumor suppressor protein inhibits cell proliferation by repression of the c-myc proto-oncogene.
evidence.snippet: We show here that RNA interference with the expression of parafibromin or Paf1 stimulates cell proliferation and increases levels of the c-myc proto-oncogene product, a DNA-binding protein and established regulator of cell growth.

evidence.reference_title: Parafibromin, product of the hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome gene HRPT2, regulates cyclin D1/PRAD1 expression.
evidence.snippet: Transient overexpression of wild-type parafibromin, but not its Leu64Pro missense mutant implicated in parathyroid cancer and familial isolated hyperparathyroidism, inhibited cell proliferation, and blocked expression of cyclin D1, a key cell cycle regulator previously implicated in parathyroid neoplasia.

evidence.reference_title: Nuclear localization of the parafibromin tumor suppressor protein implicated in the hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome enhances its proapoptotic function.
evidence.snippet: Inhibition of endogenous parafibromin expression by RNA interference inhibits the basal rate of apoptosis and apoptosis resulting from DNA damage induced by camptothecin, a topoisomerase I inhibitor.

nodes.description: Affected glands lack parafibromin protein, while normal parathyroid tissue and sporadic adenomas retain it. Parafibromin normally sits in a human PAF1 complex with PAF1, LEO1 and CTR9 that binds RNA polymerase II and links it to histone H3 lysine 4 methyltransferase activity.

evidence.reference_title: HRPT2-related familial isolated hyperparathyroidism: could molecular studies direct the surgical approach?
evidence.snippet: Using RT-PCR, mRNA transcription was altered with complete absence of both transcripts in tumor tissue. Immunohistochemical analysis of tumors showed loss of parafibromin immunoreactivity.

evidence.reference_title: Parafibromin expression, single-gland involvement, and limited parathyroidectomy in familial isolated hyperparathyroidism.
evidence.snippet: Parafibromin expression was absent in all macroscopically affected glands from FIHPT patients, but present in normal parathyroids and in adenomas arising in sporadic hyperparathyroidism.

evidence.reference_title: The parafibromin tumor suppressor protein is part of a human Paf1 complex.
evidence.snippet: By purifying cellular parafibromin and characterizing its associated proteins, we have identified a human counterpart to the yeast Paf1 complex including homologs of Leo1, Paf1, and Ctr9.

nodes.description: Renal stones are a presenting complication of the hypercalcemia; no frequency specific to CDC73-related FIHP has been reported.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic or familiar forms of primary hyperparathyroidism: description of a case series with familial isolated hyperparathyroidism and review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: A 32-year-old male patient was diagnosed with PHPT in 1999 due to joint pain, fatigue, nausea, and nephrolithiasis, which led to subsequent left nephrectomy.

nodes.description: Parafibromin-deficient chief cells expand into a parathyroid tumor. Most are single-gland adenomas, some with atypical or cystic features, and a minority are carcinomas; new tumors can arise in other glands years after surgery.

evidence.reference_title: Mice deleted for cell division cycle 73 gene develop parathyroid and uterine tumours: model for the hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumour syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Parathyroid tumours in Cdc73+/-, Cdc73+/L/PTH-Cre and Cdc73L/L/PTH-Cre mice had significantly increased proliferation, with rates >fourfold higher than that in parathyroid glands of wild-type littermates (P<0.0001).

evidence.reference_title: Parafibromin expression, single-gland involvement, and limited parathyroidectomy in familial isolated hyperparathyroidism.
evidence.snippet: Pathology confirmed single-gland involvement in all cases (11 adenomas and 1 carcinoma).

nodes.description: The usual lesion, typically single-gland; atypical and cystic adenomas occur. Second adenomas can appear in other glands years after surgery.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic analyses in patients with familial isolated hyperparathyroidism and hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumour syndrome.
evidence.snippet: One FIHP family with parathyroid carcinoma and atypical adenomas and another FIHP family with cystic parathyroid adenoma had novel frameshift mutations of 518-521del and 62-66del, respectively.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis of parathyroid tumors in familial isolated hyperparathyroidism with HRPT2 mutation: implications for cancer surveillance.
evidence.snippet: The index case, 12 yr after surgery, was normocalcemic, but ultrasonography revealed an extrathyroidal nodule in the contralateral hemithyroid tissue that proved to be atypical adenoma.

nodes.description: Parathyroid carcinoma occurs in CDC73-related FIHP kindreds, including in adolescents and young adults and in normocalcemic carriers found by surveillance, and is the main reason for lifelong follow-up. Across germline CDC73 carriers, variants disrupting the parafibromin C-terminal domain carry a higher carcinoma risk than other variants.

evidence.reference_title: CDC73 intragenic deletion in familial primary hyperparathyroidism associated with parathyroid carcinoma.
evidence.snippet: Two affected members had parathyroid carcinomas at the ages of 18 and 32 years, and they had Ki-67 proliferation indices of 5 and 14.5% and did not express parafibromin, encoded by CDC73.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis of parathyroid tumors in familial isolated hyperparathyroidism with HRPT2 mutation: implications for cancer surveillance.
evidence.snippet: a 43-yr-old normocalcemic carrier sister was found by ultrasonography to have an extrathyroidal nodule, which proved to be parathyroid carcinoma

evidence.reference_title: Surveillance for early detection of aggressive parathyroid disease: carcinoma and atypical adenoma in familial isolated hyperparathyroidism associated with a germline HRPT2 mutation.
evidence.snippet: HRPT2 mutations may be enriched in FIHP families with PT carcinoma, underscoring the importance of identifying causative mutations.

evidence.reference_title: Genotype of CDC73 germline mutation determines risk of parathyroid cancer.
evidence.snippet: The Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that high-impact mutations were associated with a 6.6-fold higher risk of parathyroid carcinoma compared to low-impact mutations, despite a similar risk of developing primary hyperparathyroidism between two groups.

nodes.description: Surgical removal of the affected gland or glands is the treatment of primary hyperparathyroidism. Limited parathyroidectomy cured most patients in one FIHP series, but recurrence after less than subtotal surgery was high in a CDC73-mutant kindred, so the extent of surgery is individualized; suspected carcinoma calls for en bloc resection. Biopsy of extrathyroidal neck tissue should be avoided because it risks seeding parathyroid tissue.

evidence.reference_title: CDC73-Related Disorders.
evidence.snippet: Parathyroidectomy is the preferred treatment for primary hyperparathyroidism, especially in individuals with HPT-JT syndrome. If parathyroid carcinoma is clinically suspected, an en bloc resection of the parathyroid gland with surrounding adherent tissue and the ipsilateral thyroid lobe should be considered.

evidence.reference_title: Parafibromin expression, single-gland involvement, and limited parathyroidectomy in familial isolated hyperparathyroidism.
evidence.snippet: Single-gland involvement often occurs; limited parathyroidectomy is effective and achieves long disease-free periods.

evidence.reference_title: HRPT2-related familial isolated hyperparathyroidism: could molecular studies direct the surgical approach?
evidence.snippet: We concluded that it is necessary to individualize the surgical approach for HRPT2-related hyperparathyroidism until we can gather a better phenotype-genotype correlation in larger series, to best define their treatment.

evidence.reference_title: CDC73-Related Disorders.
evidence.snippet: Agents/circumstances to avoid: Dehydration; radiation exposure to the neck; biopsy of extrathyroidal tissue in the neck, which increases the risk of seeding of parathyroid tissue.

nodes.description: The defining feature, occurring without the jaw, renal or uterine tumors of HPT-JT. Onset is earlier and presentation more severe than in FIHP without a CDC73 variant, and recurrence after surgery is common in some kindreds.

evidence.reference_title: CDC73-Related Disorders.
evidence.snippet: Familial isolated hyperparathyroidism (FIHP). Characterized by primary hyperparathyroidism without other associated syndromic features. Individuals with CDC73-related FIHP tend to have a more severe clinical presentation and younger age of onset than individuals with FIHP in whom a CDC73 pathogenic variant has not been identified.

evidence.reference_title: Familial isolated primary hyperparathyroidism due to HRPT2 mutation.
evidence.snippet: We present three siblings with familial isolated hyperparathyroidism due to solitary parathyroid adenoma and favorable evolution post-parathyroidectomy. Genetic tests revealed HRPT2 mutation.

evidence.reference_title: HRPT2-related familial isolated hyperparathyroidism: could molecular studies direct the surgical approach?
evidence.snippet: In this kindred there was a high prevalence of recurrence (75%), or persistence after less than subtotal parathyroidectomy

evidence.reference_title: Do Patients With Atypical Parathyroid Adenoma Need Close Follow-up?
evidence.snippet: Germline CDC73 mutation-positive patients had a higher rate of persistent/recurrent disease.

nodes.description: In the parathyroid cell that founds a tumor, an acquired frameshift, missense or other inactivating event removes the remaining CDC73 allele, completing biallelic inactivation in the Knudson pattern.
nodes.id: Somatic Second Hit on the Wild-Type CDC73 Allele

evidence.reference_title: Surveillance for early detection of aggressive parathyroid disease: carcinoma and atypical adenoma in familial isolated hyperparathyroidism associated with a germline HRPT2 mutation.
evidence.snippet: The initial tumor manifested the expected germline HRPT2 mutation, plus a distinct somatic frameshift mutation, consistent with the Knudson "two hit" concept of biallelic inactivation of a classic tumor suppressor gene.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic analyses in patients with familial isolated hyperparathyroidism and hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumour syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Biallelic inactivation of HRPT2 by a combination of germline and somatic mutation was confirmed in the parathyroid tumours.

evidence.reference_title: Parafibromin mutations in hereditary hyperparathyroidism syndromes and parathyroid tumours.
evidence.snippet: One parathyroid tumour from an FIHP patient was demonstrated to harbour a germline deletion of 1 bp together with a somatic missense (Leu95Pro) mutation, consistent with a 'two-hit' model for hereditary cancer.
